description: Geology, flooring, ancient landmarks, civil-rights history, zoology, ceremonial music and Fleet Street give this compact run an unusually varied path through science, culture, language and British history.

s05e01.description: William the Conqueror, Shakespeare, Wordsworth and Shatner are ordered by era before questions move through river banks, the tortoise and the hare, ravenous appetites, trawlers and The Sopranos. Geology later supplies igneous rock.

s05e02.description: Artemis Fowl author Eoin Colfer, Stirling Moss, Venus’s extraordinarily slow rotation and Gandhi as Time’s 1930 Person of the Year all appear in the ladder. Parquet flooring supplies the pleasingly mundane counterweight to planets, politics and motor racing.

s05e03.description: Kofi Annan, the Thunderbirds brothers being named after Mercury astronauts and an alphabetical parade of breads all precede one of the ancient world’s great landmarks: the Pharos of Alexandria.

s05e04.description: The Kansas City Chiefs, Roald Dahl’s screenwriting for Chitty Chitty Bang Bang and You Only Live Twice, major historical events and chain mail all appear before Martin Luther King Jr.’s ‘I Have a Dream’ enters the question set.

s05e05.description: British monarchs are arranged by birth before cartwheels, Casper the Friendly Ghost and The Exorcist move the ladder from royalty to the supernatural. Zoology later asks about toothed whales, completing a suitably eccentric set.

s05e06.description: Beefeaters, 101 Dalmatians, flaming Christmas pudding, RNLI lifeboats, Stannah stairlifts and election canvassing all appear before the Bridal Chorus supplies the musical flourish. It is difficult to imagine another programme assembling those nouns in one hour.

s05e07.description: Pantomime’s ‘he’s behind you’, blusher, Russell Crowe in Gladiator, jesters, knots and the mouse in ’Twas the Night Before Christmas all appear before Fleet Street brings in the history of British newspapers.
